{{Short description|none}} {{for|the other Senate election in North Dakota held in parallel|1992 United States Senate election in North Dakota}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=September 2023}} {{Infobox election | election_name = 1992 United States Senate special election in North Dakota | country = North Dakota | type = presidential | ongoing = no | previous_election = 1988 United States Senate election in North Dakota | previous_year = 1988 | next_election = 1994 United States Senate election in North Dakota | next_year = 1994 | election_date = December 4, 1992 | image1 = SenatorConrad.png | image_size = 150x150px | nominee1 = '''[[Kent Conrad]]''' | party1 = North Dakota Democratic-NPL Party | popular_vote1 = '''103,246''' | percentage1 = '''63.22%''' | image2 = File:North Dakota Lieutenant Governor Jack Dalrymple (cropped).jpg | nominee2 = [[Jack Dalrymple]] | party2 = Republican Party (United States) | popular_vote2 = 55,194 | percentage2 = 33.80% | map_image = 1992 United States Senate special election in North Dakota results map by county.svg | map_size = 250px | map_caption = County results
'''Conrad:''' {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} {{legend0|#6674de|60–70%}} {{legend0|#584cde|70–80%}}
'''Dalrymple:''' {{legend0|#FFB2B2|40–50%}} {{legend0|#E27F7F|50–60%}} | title = U.S. Senator | before_election = [[Jocelyn Burdick]] | before_party = North Dakota Democratic-NPL Party | after_election = [[Kent Conrad]] | after_party = North Dakota Democratic-NPL Party }} {{Elections in North Dakota}} The '''1992 United States Senate special election in North Dakota''' was held on December 4, 1992, to fill the [[United States Senate]] seat vacated by the late [[Quentin Burdick]]. Burdick's widow, [[Jocelyn Burdick]], was appointed as a temporary replacement until the election was held. [[North Dakota Democratic-NPL Party|Democratic-NPL]] nominee [[Kent Conrad]], who held [[North Dakota]]'s other senate seat since [[1986 United States Senate election in North Dakota|1986]], had not run for re-election to his own seat, holding himself to a campaign promise pledging to reduce the federal deficit. However, as the seat was not technically Conrad's, he opted to run for the now open seat for a second term. Conrad won the election against state representative and future Governor of North Dakota [[Jack Dalrymple]]. ==Major candidates== ===Democratic-NPL=== * [[Kent Conrad]], U.S. Senator ===Republican=== * [[Jack Dalrymple]], State Representative === Independent === Darold Larson, reverend ==Campaign== On April 2, 1992, in a surprise announcement, Kent Conrad announced he would not seek re-election to his seat, keeping a 1986 campaign promise to not run if the federal deficit had not been reduced.{{Cite news |date=1992-04-03 |title=Conrad calls it quits |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-bismarck-tribune-conrad-calls-it-qui/149619787/ |access-date=2024-06-19 |work=The Bismarck Tribune |pages=1 |quote=Kent Conrad shocked the Senate and his state by announcing Thursday he would keep a promise made six years ago not to seek re-election if the federal budget deficit was out of control. "There is only one right course and that is to keep my pledge," Conrad said in a midday speech on the Senate floor.}} However, on September 8, the state's other Senator, Quentin Burdick, died of [[heart failure]] at the age of 84.{{Cite news |date=1992-09-09 |title=N.D. senator dies |language=en |pages=3 |work=Record-Journal |agency=Associated Press |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=De1HAAAAIBAJ&dq=quentin+burdick+dies&pg=PA2&article_id=2888,1346850 |access-date=2023-09-19}} Burdick's death provided an opportunity for Conrad to remain in the Senate on the grounds that it was technically not his seat. Gov. [[George A. Sinner|George Sinner]] endorsed Conrad immediately, promising to lead a draft movement for Conrad.{{Cite news |date=1992-09-13 |title=Conrad will feel a 'draft' |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-bismarck-tribune-conrad-will-feel-a/149481444/ |access-date=2024-06-17 |work=The Bismarck Tribune |pages=1 |quote=Gov. George Sinner Saturday endorsed Sen. Kent Conrad for Quentin Burdick's U.S. Senate seat in the upcoming special election. Sinner said he'll lead a drive to draft Conrad.}} On September 21, Conrad announced his intent to seek the now open seat.{{Cite news |date=1992-09-22 |title=He will run after all |language=en |pages=A3 |work=The Vindicator |agency=Associated Press |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BUhKAAAAIBAJ&dq=kent+conrad+not+run&pg=PA14&article_id=5503,3150008 |access-date=2023-09-19}} On October 4, he officially became the Democratic nominee.{{Cite news |date=1992-10-05 |title=2 nominated for seat of late N. Dakota senator |language=en |pages=3A |work=The News |agency=Associated Press |location=Boca Raton, FL |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=hOg0AAAAIBAJ&dq=kent+conrad+nominated&pg=PA2&article_id=2554,2614931 |access-date=2023-09-19}} On the Republican side, there had initially been an attempt to draft former senator [[Mark Andrews (politician)|Mark Andrews]] for the race.{{Cite news |last=Cole |first=Janell |date=1992-09-16 |title=Draft Andrews drive is official |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-bismarck-tribune-draft-andrews-drive/149620866/ |access-date=2024-06-19 |work=The Bismarck Tribune |pages=1 |quote=A committee of more than 50 Republicans announced Tuesday they are beginning a campaign to draft former Republican Sen. Mark Andrews to run for the unexpired term of the late Sen. Quentin Burdick. Burdick died of heart failure Sept. 8.}} Andrews would ultimately decline on September 26, opting to spend time with his family.{{Cite news |last=Voskul |first=Vicki |date=1992-09-27 |title=Andrews says no, GOP field widens |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-bismarck-tribune-andrews-says-no-go/149620906/ |access-date=2024-06-19 |work=The Bismarck Tribune |pages=1 |quote=Former North Dakota senator Mark Andrews ended speculation about a state Republican Party nomination for the U.S. Senate on Saturday by saying, "'no' to North Dakota", and "'yes' to my family."}} The Republican nominee would be Jack Dalrymple, a state representative who ran concurrently in this race with his own re-election campaign.{{Cite news |last=Wetzel |first=Dale |date=1992-12-05 |title=Democrat Conrad is victor in last U.S. Senate Election |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=y8hJAAAAIBAJ&dq=kent+conrad+special+election&pg=PA6&article_id=5034,5168157 |access-date=2023-09-19 |work=The Madison Courier |pages=B3 |language=en}} He defeated financial planner David Vanderscoff with 426 votes to 126.{{Cite news |date=1992-10-05 |title=Dalrymple wins bid |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-bismarck-tribune-dalrymple-wins-bid/149621091/ |access-date=2024-06-19 |work=The Bismarck Tribune |pages=1 |quote=Jack Dalrymple, Casselton farmer and state legislator, won the Republican endorsement Sunday in Bismarck for the late Quentin Burdick's U.S. Senate seat, prevailing over Bismarck financial planner David Vanderscoff 426 delegate votes to 126.}} Dalrymple saw Conrad's run as a breach of his promise in spirit if not letter. He contended that Conrad had intended to run for Burdick's seat the whole time, and Conrad was a liar.{{Cite web |date=2015-05-26 |title=Democrat Wins Senate Seat in North Dakota - NYTimes.com |website=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1992/12/05/us/democrat-wins-senate-seat-in-north-dakota.html |access-date=2023-08-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150526052637/https://www.nytimes.com/1992/12/05/us/democrat-wins-senate-seat-in-north-dakota.html |archive-date=May 26, 2015 }} Among other issues, Dalrymple argued in favor of a plan that would guarantee farmers $5 for a bushel of wheat, a plan which Conrad criticized as unrealistic. Dalrymple also tried to attack Conrad for indicating a willingness to cut Medicare in a debate, though Conrad contended he only intended to reduce costs via reform.{{Cite news |date=1992-12-04 |title=Last Senate campaign ends today |language=en |pages=8A |work=The Albany Herald |agency=Associated Press |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=oi9DAAAAIBAJ&dq=jack+dalrymple+conrad&pg=PA5&article_id=3008,381099 |access-date=2023-09-19}} A third candidate was Darold Larson, a reverend who ran an anti-abortion campaign, including airing a graphic ad showing aborted fetuses.{{Cite news |date=1992-12-06 |title=Conrad wins nation's last U.S. Senate seat |language=en |pages=2C |work=The Victoria Advocate |agency=The Associated Press |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xTMhAAAAIBAJ&dq=darold+larson+1992&pg=PA36&article_id=7272,1239184 |access-date=2023-09-19}} Ultimately Conrad's high name recognition approval ratings as Senator carried through and he was seen as the clear favorite to secure victory against Dalrymple.{{Cite web |title=Our Campaigns - ND US Senate - Special Election Race - Dec 04, 1992 |url=https://www.ourcampaigns.com/RaceDetail.html?RaceID=3434 |access-date=2023-08-26 |website=www.ourcampaigns.com}}{{Cite news |date=1992-11-30 |title=North Dakota senator favored in special vote |language=en |pages=3 |work=Toledo Blade |agency=Toledo Blade Wire Service |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=61ZPAAAAIBAJ&dq=jack+dalrymple+conrad&pg=PA2&article_id=5134,9114575 |access-date=2023-09-19}} As a result, the biggest concern for both campaigns was getting their supporters to vote due to apathy.{{Cite news |last=Wetzel |first=Dale |date=1992-12-05 |title=Men fight in last Senate race of '92 |language=en |pages=5B |work=Moscow-Pullman Daily News |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=VsMjAAAAIBAJ&dq=kent+conrad+jack+dalrymple+about&pg=PA27&article_id=2208,2575988 |access-date=2023-09-19}} Conrad won decisively, albeit with lower turnout statewide, in part due to election fatigue and cold weather.{{Cite news |date=2006-12-06 |title=14 years ago, Wednesday December 9, 1992 |language=en |pages=2 |work=The New Salem Journal |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=8U05AAAAIBAJ&dq=kent+conrad+special+election&pg=PA2&article_id=2465,2115036 |access-date=2023-09-19}}{{Cite web |title=Conrad wins special election for another Senate seat - UPI Archives |url=https://www.upi.com/Archives/1992/12/04/Conrad-wins-special-election-for-another-Senate-seat/5728723445200/ |access-date=2023-08-26 |website=UPI |language=en}} === Debate === [https://www.c-span.org/video/?35376-1/north-dakota-senate-debate# Complete video of debate], November 27, 1992 ==Results== {{Election box begin | title = General election results[https://vip.sos.nd.gov/pdfs/Abstracts%20by%20Year/1990%20through%201998%20Statewide%20Election%20Results/1992%20Special%20Election/Special%20Election%2012-04-1992.pdf Results] nd.go}} {{Election box winning candidate with party link | party = North Dakota Democratic-NPL Party | candidate = [[Kent Conrad]] | votes = 103,246 | percentage = 63.22 | change = +3.77 }} {{Election box candidate with party link|party=Republican Party (United States)|candidate=[[Jack Dalrymple]]|votes=55,194|percentage=33.80|change= -5.26}} {{Election box candidate with party link|party=Independent (United States)|candidate=Darold Larson|votes=4,871|percentage=2.98|change=N/A}} {{Election box majority|votes=48,052|percentage=|change=}} {{Election box turnout|votes=163,311|percentage=|change=}} {{Election box hold with party link | winner = North Dakota Democratic-NPL Party | loser = | swing = }} {{Election box end}} ==See also== * [[1992 United States Senate elections]] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== * [http://www.ourcampaigns.com/RaceDetail.html?RaceID=3434 1992 Special North Dakota U.S. Senate Election results] {{North Dakota elections}} {{United States elections, 1992}} [[Category:1992 United States Senate elections|North Dakota]] [[Category:United States Senate elections in North Dakota|1992]] [[Category:United States Senate special elections|North Dakota 1992]] [[Category:1992 elections in North Dakota]] [[Category:Special elections to the 102nd United States Congress|North Dakota 1992]] [[Category:Special elections in North Dakota|United States Senate 1992]]
